public_rationale: Two of the three parts hold. CNBC reported that Sutskever and Leike announced their departures on X on Tuesday, May 14, 2024 (e2). On May 17, 2024, CNBC confirmed that OpenAI had disbanded its team focused on long-term AI risks (e1). Fortune reported the same day, citing Bloomberg, that the Superalignment team led by Leike and Sutskever had been dissolved (e3). Both events fall within the week before the May 21 post. The third part, that OpenAI 'repeatedly lied' about the Sky voice, is not established. The Washington Post reported on May 22, 2024 that the Sky actor was hired months before Altman contacted Johansson, according to documents, recordings, casting directors and the actor's agent (e4). That supports OpenAI's account of how Sky was cast. But it does not settle what OpenAI intended or knew, and the evidence in this case does not show that OpenAI's statements were knowingly false. So two parts are supported and the lying part remains unsettled.
limitations: The lying part turns on intent and knowledge. The evidence in this case does not show either.
The Washington Post's casting evidence dates from 2023, outside the claim's one-week window. It bears only on whether the May 2024 statements were accurate.
The Superalignment team was one of several safety-related groups at OpenAI. The case reads 'its AI safety team' as that team.

'Repeatedly lied about a voice product' is the same allegation as the Sky claims graded separately. It requires showing that OpenAI's statements were knowingly false.
criteria.support_condition: Reports showing Sutskever and Leike resigned and the Superalignment team was dissolved between about May 13 and May 21, 2024, plus evidence that OpenAI's Sky statements in that window were knowingly false.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that the resignations or the dissolution did not happen in that week, or that OpenAI's Sky statements were accurate.
